description: Panels for the riAuth series in deploy/riauth-alerts.yml. Request error rate, request latency, rate limits, worker rejections, and the queue gauges are rendered by src/api/observability.rs. Signing errors, cleanup errors, and storage write wait are rendered by src/telemetry.rs. A disposable loopback import of this file is recorded in docs/roadmap/o06-grafana-loopback.md. Each queue gauge is one series per queue label. pending and failed are index aggregates, and a retry can be counted in both. Oldest pending age is the scrape time minus the earliest timestamp in the age index for a pending row. That timestamp is created_at, and logout, mail, provisioning jobs, and SSF use plan.expires_at minus 3600 seconds when created_at is absent. Connector lag, key problems, and readiness are left unplotted.

options.content:
These panels repeat the PromQL in deploy/riauth-alerts.yml. A disposable loopback import of this file is recorded in docs/roadmap/o06-grafana-loopback.md.

Request error rate, request latency, rate limits, and worker rejections are unlabeled series rendered by src/api/observability.rs. Signing errors, cleanup errors, and storage write wait are unlabeled series rendered by src/telemetry.rs. Counters and histograms are process-local and reset when the process starts. Each scraped instance is its own series.

Queue gauges are one series per queue label: logout_deliveries, mail_deliveries, provisioning_jobs, ssf_deliveries, offboard_jobs, provisioning_deactivations. The alert rules compare each series on its own. pending and failed are maintained index counters, and a retry can be counted in both. Oldest pending age is the scrape time minus the earliest timestamp in the age index for a pending row. That timestamp is created_at, and logout, mail, provisioning jobs, and SSF use plan.expires_at minus 3600 seconds when created_at is absent. Connector lag, key problems, and readiness are left unplotted.

panels.description: Unlabeled 5xx responses divided by unlabeled requests, using the alert rule's five-minute rate and clamp_min. 401 and 429 responses stay in the denominator. The combined response-error counter is a separate series.
panels.title: Server error rate

panels.description: 95th percentile of the unlabeled riauth_request_duration_seconds histogram rendered by src/api/observability.rs. The route histogram riauth_http_duration_seconds is a separate labelled series. The alert line is one second.
panels.title: Request latency

panels.description: Five-minute rate of unlabeled riauth_rate_limited_total. The counter increments on HTTP 429. The alert line is one rejection per second.
panels.title: Rate-limit rejections

panels.description: Five-minute rate of unlabeled riauth_worker_rejections_total. The counter increments when a foreground request finds the application worker permits occupied. The alert fires when this rate is above zero.
panels.title: Worker rejections

panels.description: Five-minute increase of riauth_signing_errors_total, rendered by src/telemetry.rs. The counter is process-local and resets when the process starts. The alert fires when this increase is above zero.
panels.title: Signing errors

panels.description: Ten-minute increase of riauth_cleanup_errors_total, rendered by src/telemetry.rs. The counter is process-local and resets when the process starts. The alert fires when this increase is above zero.
panels.title: Cleanup errors

panels.description: 95th percentile of the unlabeled riauth_storage_write_wait_seconds histogram rendered by src/telemetry.rs. The activity-labelled write-wait histogram is a separate series. The alert line is 500 milliseconds. The histogram is process-local.
panels.title: Storage write wait

panels.description: Gauge riauth_queue_pending. One series per queue label. The backlog rule compares this series with the same queue's oldest pending age and does not sum queues. logout_deliveries, mail_deliveries, provisioning_jobs, and ssf_deliveries count a row pending when it is not delivered, not stopped, and not completed, so a retry stays pending. offboard_jobs counts scheduled and running. provisioning_deactivations counts pending and running. The value is the maintained index counter, read from the store at scrape time.
panels.title: Queue pending

panels.description: Gauge riauth_queue_failed. One series per queue label. The alert fires for each series above zero. For logout_deliveries, mail_deliveries, provisioning_jobs, and ssf_deliveries, failed includes a stopped or stale row, last_failed, a next_attempt of u64::MAX, a stored error, a non-2xx last_status, and an undelivered unleased mail row that already has an attempt. A retry can be pending and failed together, so ssf_deliveries folds retrying, stopped, and cancelled into this gauge. offboard_jobs counts status failed only. provisioning_deactivations counts failed and stale.
panels.title: Queue failed

panels.description: Gauge riauth_queue_oldest_pending_seconds. At scrape time this is now minus the earliest timestamp in that queue's age index. The index lists pending rows. Offboarding jobs and deactivations store created_at. Logout, mail, provisioning jobs, and SSF store created_at, and when that field is absent they store plan.expires_at minus 3600 seconds. The age index is distinct from the due timestamp. The backlog rule is this gauge above 300 seconds while the same queue's pending gauge is above zero.
panels.title: Queue oldest pending age
